name: browser-memory
description: A reusable memory of web actions: learn an action once, replay it deterministically forever.
long_description:
browser-memory gives an agent a memory of the web actions it already knows how to do. The first time an action is performed on a site it is learned and saved as an executable tool; the next time it is discovered and replayed deterministically, with no model in the loop.

It drives its own dedicated Chrome (its own persistent profile, its own internal debugging port) — it never touches your real browser. You log into a site by hand once and that session survives every later run.

The memory lives on disk in ~/.tool-memory and is shared across every client you install this in.

tools.name: discover
tools.description: Search the memory for tools that already solve a goal on a site.

tools.name: run
tools.description: Replay a saved tool or composite deterministically and return structured data.

tools.name: request
tools.description: Freeze the trace of a new web action so it can be distilled into a reusable tool.

tools.name: save
tools.description: Validate and persist a distilled tool.

tools.name: list_sites
tools.description: List the sites the memory has tools for.

tools.name: forget_site
tools.description: Delete every tool learned for a site.

tools.name: bm_navigate
tools.description: Open a URL in the dedicated Chrome.

tools.name: bm_snapshot
tools.description: Read the page as an accessibility tree with refs.

tools.name: bm_type
tools.description: Type into an element by ref.

home.title: Memory folder
home.description: Where your learned tools, index, traces and the dedicated Chrome profile live. Leave it empty to use ~/.tool-memory, which is what every other client uses — that's how one memory is shared across all of them.

registry_enabled.title: Use the shared registry
registry_enabled.description: Pull community tools from the remote registry. Turn off for a 100% local memory.

registry_url.title: Registry URL
registry_url.description: Backend the shared registry points at. Leave as is unless you self-host.
